svg.title: Reading one tool result: the isError branch and every content block type
svg.desc: A decision flow starting at a call to call_tool. The first question asks whether the call raised, and a yes leads right to a red box: a transport or protocol fault, the process died or JSON-RPC refused the message. The second question asks whether is_error is true on the returned result, read before any content is touched, and a yes leads right to a second red box: the tool ran and failed, on a response whose resultType is still complete, over HTTP 200, where nothing raised so nothing caught it. Both red boxes converge on one box saying there is a single failed outcome either way, carrying an ok flag of false and a rendering that begins TOOL FAILED. The no path leads to a green box saying the tool succeeded and that an absent flag and a false flag mean the same thing. Below a rule, the payload is split into two fields: structured content, present when the tool declares an output schema and allowed to be any JSON value rather than only an object, and content, which is required but may be empty and whose blocks must be dispatched on their type, because reading the text attribute off every block silently drops four of the five members. Content fans out into six branches: text used as it stands, image and audio described by mime type rather than inlined, a resource link treated as a pointer rather than the content, an embedded resource inlined when it is text and described when it is a blob, and a dashed sixth branch for a type from a newer server, which becomes a placeholder and never a crash. All six converge on one outcome object, described as the same type the failed path produced.
svg.text: Two failure paths that look nothing alike on the wire. Then six content branches, not one.
